evals.prompt: First run. T3 Code's settings.json lists favorites claude-opus-5-5 (claudeAgent), gpt-6.1-sol (codex) and gemini-4-neon (antigravity). There is no classification file yet. fleet-plan is about to ask its question batch.
evals.expected_output: Reads favorites from settings.json without writing to it. Proposes intelligence, taste, cost and a best-use line for all three, says which ratings are guesses, shows one table, and puts a single accept-or-edit question into fleet-plan's batch instead of asking separately. Saves ~/.config/t3-linear-fleet/models.json with one entry per model and today's date, and reads it back.

evals.prompt: The classification file rates claude-opus-5-5, gpt-6.1-sol and gemini-4-neon. The user has since removed gemini-4-neon from favorites and added claude-fable-5-2.
evals.expected_output: Marks gemini-4-neon favorite:false and keeps its ratings. Asks only about claude-fable-5-2, with proposed defaults. Does not re-ask about Opus or Sol and does not change their ratings.

evals.prompt: During fleet-run, ticket ENG-40 names a model that no machine offers. Classified favorites: model A (intelligence 9, taste 8), model B (intelligence 8, taste 9), model C (intelligence 6, taste 6). ENG-40's model was rated intelligence 9, taste 9. A new favorite D is not classified yet.
evals.expected_output: Swaps ENG-40 to model A (smallest intelligence difference, then taste), logs the swap, and does not ask the user to classify D mid-run; D is listed as unclassified in the final report.

evals.prompt: models.json rates claude-fable-5-2 (intelligence 9, taste 9, cost 2) with "replacedBy": {"model": "claude-opus-5-5", "effort": "high"}, and claude-opus-5-5 (intelligence 8, taste 8, cost 4). Both are T3 Code favorites offered by a usable provider, and they are the only candidates. fleet-plan is choosing a model for a t3-fleet-risky money ticket (the highest-intelligence rule, normally xhigh or max), and an ordinary implementation ticket (intelligence 7+, then highest cost score, medium). fleet-run later finds an older ticket whose Fleet section says Model: claude-fable-5-2, Effort: xhigh. The run request says nothing about effort.
evals.expected_output: Fable is ranked like any candidate but never runs. The risky ticket's rule picks Fable (intelligence 9), so fleet-plan writes Model: claude-opus-5-5, Effort: high (the replacement effort, not xhigh). The ordinary ticket's rule picks Opus on its own ratings (cost 4 beats Fable's 2), so it gets claude-opus-5-5 at medium. fleet-run runs the older ticket on claude-opus-5-5 at high, logs the swap, and does not ask. Fable keeps favorite:true and its ratings; replacedBy stays as the user set it. No reviewer is ever Fable.
